chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Salt narrated to me, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Khalid, on the authority of Mansur ibn al-Abbas, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jinah, on the authority of Mutfir, the freedman of Ma'an, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There are three things for the believer in which there is comfort: a spacious house that conceals his private parts and his bad state from people; a virtuous wife who assists him in the affairs of this world and the Hereafter; and a daughter or a sister who leaves his house either by death or by marriage.
ai.seo_question: What are the three things that bring comfort to a believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three elements as foundational pillars of domestic tranquility, emphasizing the social and spiritual necessity of privacy (khusūṣiyyah), marital partnership, and the natural progression of family life. This triad reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing worldly stability with religious duty, where the home serves as a sanctuary for worship and the family unit as a support system for spiritual growth. The mention of a daughter or sister specifically underscores the protective role of female kin in maintaining household harmony until their transition to their own families.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-206 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Salt quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Khalid, on the authorityof Mansoor ibn al-Ab’bas, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jinah, on the authority of Motrif - a servant of Ma’an, that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“There are three things which comfort a believer: a big house in which he guards his privacy and his bad states of health from the people; a good wife who assists him in the affairs of this life and the Hereafter; and a daughter or a sister who leaves his house either by death or because of marriage.”
